description: First KYA ruleset. 18 rules active (checkable against the current corpus/schema/registry data), 15 draft (real rule, but blocked on a registry or schema piece that doesn't exist yet — see each rule's notes). Promoting a draft rule to active is PLAN item 14 work, not this file's job.

rules.description: The credential's issuer_id must exist in data/registry/issuers.json. An issuer_id absent entirely has no standing whatsoever (registry_notes: at least as severe as an explicit revocation).

The issuer's status must be 'active' as of the credential's issued_at — point-in-time, not a snapshot check. A credential issued before the issuer's revoked_at is unaffected; one issued on or after it is invalid regardless of signature validity (issuers.json, Svaneti Digital Trust example).

The issuer's trust_level must be at least 'recognized'. Every issuer in the current registry is 'primary' or 'recognized', so this rule has no bite yet — it exists so a future lower-tier issuer status (e.g. 'provisional') has somewhere to land.

The issuer's accredited_since must be within this many days of the ruleset's as_of date. Every active issuer in the current registry was accredited within the last ~9 months, so this rule has no bite yet either (same honest situation as KYA-ISS-03) — it exists so an issuer that's gone a long time without re-accreditation has somewhere to surface, rather than being trusted indefinitely off a single point-in-time check.
expires_at must be in the future relative to the case's activity window. A short grace period absorbs clock-skew/renewal-in-flight noise without masking a genuinely lapsed credential.

issued_at to expires_at must span at least this many days. Every credential in the current corpus runs a full year; an unusually short-lived credential is a throwaway/synthetic-identity signal worth flagging even when everything else checks out.

issued_at must strictly precede expires_at. A basic well-formedness guard: a credential where these are equal, reversed, or otherwise nonsensical shouldn't be treated as validly dated just because both fields are present.
When an agent's credential is re-issued, the new one should not have overlapping validity with the old one — no window where two credentials for the same agent are simultaneously valid.
rules.notes: The corpus carries exactly one credential per case/agent, with no re-issuance history to compare against. Needs multi-issuance corpus support (or a live credential-history store in production) before this is evaluable. Draft pending that.

rules.description: signature.alg must be on the allow-list. Only Ed25519 is accepted anywhere in this system today (schemas/common.py pins the same literal at the type level).

The credential's signature must cryptographically verify against the issuer's public key in data/registry/keystore.json. A forged or corrupted signature is a maximal-severity finding on its own, independent of anything else about the credential.
signed_payload_hash must equal the real SHA-256 of the credential's own canonical content (data/canonical.py). A mismatch means the credential was altered after it was signed.

The last entry in delegation_chain must have holder_type == 'human'. This is the core KYA differentiator from a plain signature check: the AP2 red-teaming cited in the concept note showed a fully valid, signed mandate whose decision-making was still compromised — every credential checked out, but there was no accountable human at the end of the chain.

No holder_id may appear more than once across delegation_chain levels. A repeated holder is a structural anomaly (a cycle, or an id reused to pad apparent chain depth) regardless of whether every individual signature verifies.

delegation_chain length must not exceed this depth. Every valid case in the current corpus runs 2-3 levels; depth itself is a risk factor independent of validity, since a longer chain is harder to supervise even when every link checks out.

Each delegation_chain entry's own self-attestation signature ({level, holder_id, holder_type, name}) must verify against that holder's key. The chain-terminates-in-human check (KYA-DEL-01) is meaningless if the entries along the way aren't themselves authentic.

The human at the end of the delegation chain should be the same principal_id as the Intent mandate's principal. In every compliant case in the current corpus these match by construction; a mismatch means the person accountable for the agent's identity and the person who actually authorized this specific mandate are two different humans, which is a structural inconsistency worth its own finding even when both individually check out.

Every holder_type == 'agent' entry in the delegation chain (not just the credential's own agent_id) should itself resolve to a known, registered agent — an unregistered intermediate hop is exactly as opaque to supervision as an unregistered primary agent.
rules.notes: Distinct from KYA-AGT-01 (which is about the primary agent_id): this checks every intermediate agent-type hop, not just the credential subject. Blocked on the same missing agent registry as KYA-AGT-01 — draft until that exists.

rules.description: The human terminating the delegation chain should be cross-checked against the operator firm's list of authorized signatories, not just accepted as 'any named human'. KYA-DEL-05 already confirms this human matches the Intent's own principal; this rule adds an independent, firm-side check that the same person is actually entitled to authorize agents for that firm.
rules.notes: Needs a firms registry with a signatory list, which doesn't exist yet (same blocker as the KYA-OPF family). Draft until that exists.

rules.description: Every string in capabilities must match a known prefix or an exact known value. Observed vocabulary across the current corpus: payment_initiation:<category>, vendor_lookup:<scope>, and the bare value cart_construction.
capabilities must be non-empty. A credential attesting no scopes at all is either malformed or trivially over-broad in practice (nothing to check a transaction against), and shouldn't pass silently.
The credential's capabilities should be a superset of what the Intent's authorization_scope.purpose_category actually needs.
rules.notes: Needs a purpose_category -> required-capabilities mapping table that doesn't exist yet. Evaluating this correctly is agents/kya.py logic (PLAN item 5), not something a ruleset param alone can encode well; draft until that mapping is designed.

rules.description: An agent's capability set growing across successive credential re-issuances, faster than its declared purpose has changed, is a least-privilege signal worth surfacing even before any capability has actually been misused.
rules.notes: Same blocker as KYA-CRD-04: needs re-issuance history per agent, which the corpus doesn't carry (one credential per case). Draft pending multi-issuance corpus/registry support.

rules.description: consent.method on the Intent mandate must be on the allow-list of acceptable consent-capture methods. Every case in the current corpus uses in_app_biometric, so like KYA-ISS-03/04 this has no bite on the corpus today — it exists so a weaker or unrecognized consent method (e.g. an unauthenticated web form) has somewhere to land instead of being silently accepted.
The same signer_key_id should not attest for more than one distinct human/agent/org identity across the corpus.
rules.notes: Per-case KYA evaluation only sees one case at a time; this check needs a corpus-wide (or registry-wide, in production) key-usage index, which is ingestion/registry infrastructure that doesn't exist yet (PLAN item 3+). Draft until that index exists.

rules.description: The same credential_id should not appear on more than one distinct agent_id — a reused credential_id is a structural anomaly independent of whether any individual credential's signature verifies.
rules.notes: Same blocker as KYA-SEC-01: needs a corpus-wide/registry-wide index, not per-case visibility. Draft until that exists. (All 7 credential_ids in the current corpus are already distinct, so this wouldn't currently fire even if active — but that's the corpus being clean, not the check being implemented.)

rules.description: operator_firm must match a known, onboarded firm entity.
rules.notes: No firms registry exists yet (only data/registry/issuers.json). Draft until a firms.json equivalent is built — out of scope for PLAN item 2, which is KYA rules specifically, not new corpus data.

rules.description: The operator firm itself (not just the agent) must not be suspended or under investigation — the KYC analogue of screening the legal entity, not only the credential it issued.
rules.notes: Depends on the same firms registry as KYA-OPF-01. Draft until that exists.

rules.description: The operator firm should have a named accountable person on file for its agent fleet's behavior, the way a compliance officer exists today.
rules.notes: Depends on the same firms registry as KYA-OPF-01/02. Draft until that exists.

rules.description: If the operator firm's ownership/control has changed since a credential was issued, that credential's continued validity is worth re-examining rather than assumed — the entity that was vetted at issuance may no longer be the entity actually operating the agent.
rules.notes: Depends on the same firms registry as KYA-OPF-01/02/03, plus an ownership-history field that registry would also need to carry. Draft until both exist.

rules.description: An agent should exist in an agent registry before any credential involving it is even evaluated — registration as a distinct step, not something a credential's mere existence implies.
rules.notes: Current schema conflates 'credential' with 'registration' (schemas/kya.py has no separate agent-registry concept). A real gap, not just missing data — needs a schema decision, not only a new JSON file. Draft pending that design.

rules.description: The credential should declare an agent classification/type (e.g. shopping, bill-pay, advisory) so risk weighting can vary by agent type rather than treating every agent identically.
rules.notes: schemas/kya.py::KYACredential has no classification field yet. Draft until that schema field is added and the corpus is updated to carry it.

rules.description: A mandate's validity should be conditioned on the agent's model_version matching what the credential attests — an unexplained model swap changes the agent's actual behavior without a fresh human authorization event.
rules.notes: model_version currently lives only on Intent.agent (schemas/mandate.py::AgentInfo), not on KYACredential, so there's nothing on the credential side to pin against, and the corpus only carries one credential snapshot per case (no re-issuance history to compare across). Draft pending both a schema field and multi-issuance corpus support.

rules.description: The agent's model_version must not be on a registry-maintained blocklist of recalled or known-unsafe versions — the agent-identity analogue of a product recall, so a version flagged unsafe after issuance doesn't keep transacting silently.
rules.notes: No model-version blocklist registry exists yet. Draft until one is built; would live alongside data/registry/issuers.json as another versioned registry file.
